title: Conditional Flow-VAE for Safety-Critical Traffic Scenario Generation

control_signal.value: Difficulty/maneuver label (nominal, intermediate, challenging) from automatically generated heuristic labels, plus the number of flow timesteps used at inference.

control_mechanism.value: A conditional flow-matching transformer transports frozen CVAE prior latents from the nominal to the safety-critical distribution; the label conditions the flow model, and decoding intermediate flow steps gives partial criticality.

base_model.value: Conditional VAE (per-actor latents) plus a flow-matching transformer; shared transformer backbone with actor-map, actor-actor and actor-time attention; decoder predicts steering and acceleration.

datasets.value: In-house self-driving dataset, about 20,000 20 s scenarios (highway and urban): about 10,000 real logs, 10,000 simulated safety-critical, plus about 500 mined real safety-critical snippets; 20% of real safety-critical held out.

metrics.value: Realism: distribution JSD (speed, acceleration, jerk), displacement error. Criticality/safety: minSTTC, near-miss rate (minSTTC under 3 s), scenario collision rate.

controllability_evidence.value: Table IV: from nominal to challenging label, minSTTC falls from 3.263 to 1.967 and near-miss rate rises from 0.281 to 0.500; more flow timesteps gives more safety-critical rollouts.

stated_limitations.value: Real data curation and synthetic generation are proof-of-concept; sim-to-real fidelity could improve (friction); control is over degree of criticality, not the specific maneuver, left to future work.

notes: Control is mainly via latent flow transport; the label conditioning is a trained-in input, so could also be read as conditioning inputs. Near-miss unit is shown as fraction in Table IV but as percent in Table II.
